newsitem.title: USA: USDA sees fed cattle marketing up 3 pct in Q1 1997.
newsitem.headline: USDA sees fed cattle marketing up 3 pct in Q1 1997.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department forecast fed cattle marketings would rise about three percent in the first quarter of 1997 from a year earlier, as the large late summer and early fall placements were marketed.

In a monthly outlook report, USDA's Economic Research Service (ERS) said a more normal placement pattern in 1997 might slightly reduce second-quarter marketings from the large 1996 levels, but said marketings in the second half could then rise five to seven percent from the low second-half 1996 levels.

ERS said for all 1997, beef production could be up about two percent, the same output increase as in 1996, but said the slaughter mix will shift to a larger porportion of fed cattle and thus heavier average cattle slaughter weights.
Fed cattle prices are expected to average in the mid-$60's in the late fall through much of 1997 as fed beef supplies rise, USDA's research arm said.
It predicted that bigger supplies, an uncertain export market and larger supplies of competing meats at relatively lower prices would hold down price gains.
"Feeder steer prices will return to a premium over fed cattle prices, but not until next year's grain crop is safely in the ground and forage supplies are replenished," it said.
